PullRequest.Title: agentHost: hash custom tool names in telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Prevents custom MCP and third-party tool names from being recorded verbatim in Agent Host product telemetry. Recognized code-defined names remain readable; other names become deterministic SHA-256 identifiers. For example, `bash` remains `bash`, while an unrecognized tool name becomes a lowercase hexadecimal digest.

Normalize names centrally in the telemetry reporter for tool invocation, approval, stall/recovery, and turn-hang events. Safety does not depend on the reported tool source: MCP and unknown tools can arrive with agent-host provenance.

AHP does not expose the runtime's per-tool `safeForTelemetry` declaration, so the reporter uses a conservative exact-name allowlist for known Copilot, Claude, Codex, and host tools. Historical data cleanup and separate workbench/extension telemetry producers are outside this patch.

### Validation

Completed on the patch before rebasing cleanly onto the latest `main`:

- `node build\next\index.ts transpile` - passed.
- `node .\node_modules\@typescript\native\bin\tsc --project .\src\tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck` - passed.
- `node .\node_modules\mocha\bin\mocha.js .\test\unit\node\index.js --delay --ui=tdd --exit --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostTelemetryReporter.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostToolCallTelemetry.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostTurnHangTelemetry.test.ts --reporter dot` - 81 tests passed.

The regression cases exercise all six event boundaries with MCP, client, misclassified agent-host, and unknown sources, including prefix lookalikes and hash-shaped custom names. The standard Electron test launcher was blocked by the local pnpm launcher; the focused suites passed using the repository's Node runner.

Scenarios.Scenario: Complete tool calls, including deferred model attribution and turn-end flushing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentSideEffects handles ChatToolCallComplete synchronously. AgentHostToolCallTracker either reports immediately or queues until model attribution/session cleanup. The added name hash runs synchronously when reporting, but collector delivery is not awaited and cannot delay progress through network latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clean, clone and flatten existing event data for telemetry appenders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two telemetry records per reported tool call, with validation for the configured appenders. Custom toolId values are now fixed 64-character digests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two records and appender transformations were produced using the original name.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing synchronous event preparation; the diff adds only hashing the identifier, not another record or full-result serialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue events in the existing collector and POST collector payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 2N records feed SDK-managed payload grouping; POST count depends on payload limits, scheduling and retries, not one request per tool. No added events or requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical collector path and event count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous, fire-and-forget transport; not awaited by the reporter.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write telemetry trace records to the existing local rotating logger when trace logging is enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two trace records per reported call when enabled; native logger buffering and rotation are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same trace-record count, with the original tool name.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing logging submission; no newly added flush or awaited disk operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N completed tool calls with ordinary identifier-sized names. Completion consumes the tracking entry, suppressing duplicate reports. Each custom name is hashed once per invocation report and reused for the two existing telemetry events; tool results and the available-tool collection are not hashed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hashing and event construction execute on the host's JavaScript thread. Deferred reports may flush in a synchronous loop, as before. Existing PostChannel sends asynchronously; its SDK-owned batching/concurrency policy is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The fixed allowlist is initialized once and checked with Set.has. Custom hashes are not cached across invocations, but the same result serves both invocation events. Existing pending reports are removed before flushing. Collector initialization is coalesced through _asyncAiCore.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the traced per-report hash, reuse across both events, duplicate suppression, deferred flushing and unchanged transport paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No runtime timing measurements were taken. Invocation volume and name lengths vary; realistic tool identifiers do not establish substantial hashing latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added work is a small identifier hash, not collection-wide work, extra boundary fan-out or unbounded retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Report Copilot tool approval after permission completion or a tool with no permission request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CopilotAgentSession reports approval from permission/tool lifecycle callbacks. The added hash executes synchronously before callback continuation. Existing telemetry submission does not await network or filesystem completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct and sanitize the existing chat.toolApproval record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One record per eligible, deduplicated approval report.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same record was constructed with report.toolId unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous preparation; only the tool identifier is newly hashed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send existing approval records through collector-managed payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One enqueued record per approval, grouped with other telemetry; no new POST per approval.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same collector transport, grouping and event frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the callback's awaited critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit the existing approval trace record to the local logger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One trace record per approval when trace logging is enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No new disk flush or wait.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One approval report per eligible tool call, guarded by the approval record's reported flag. No normalization occurs on streamed tool-call deltas.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous SDK callback processing on the host thread; collector transport remains asynchronous and SDK-managed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fixed allowlist lookup; no hash-result cache or growing name map. Approval deduplication and record ownership are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from permission-completion and tool-start callers, the reported guard and the reporter/service implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Hash duration was not measured, but inputs are tool names rather than arguments, outputs or entire schemas.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression; bounded per-approval privacy normalization does not change event frequency or introduce an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Diagnose stalled tool calls, their completion, and quiet turns
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing five-minute tool-stall and turn-hang timers invoke reporting. Recovery is reported during tool completion. Only the selected tool name is normalized; no additional diagnostic read, client query or provider call is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare and sanitize the existing stall, recovery and hang records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing event per eligible stall, recovery or deduplicated hang reason, with at most one tool-name hash per event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical records, diagnostic snapshots and deduplication using original names.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in existing diagnostic callbacks or completion handling; not in rendering or input processing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send diagnostic records through the existing collector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing diagnostic event count; requests are grouped by collector payloads and retry policy, not by number of in-flight tools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same network path, cardinality and scheduling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delivery is not awaited by timer or completion callbacks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit diagnostic trace records to the existing rotating logger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One trace record per emitted diagnostic event when enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same trace events and logger lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing submission only, without a newly introduced flush.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S stalled tool calls produce existing stall records and at most one paired completion each. Turn hangs are deduplicated per reason, with at most six quiet-window checks before activity resets them. Even with many in-flight tools, a hang report hashes only the selected stuck tool, not every tool.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Timer callbacks and recovery processing run synchronously on the host event loop. Independent sessions can report in the same period, but no new asynchronous tasks or global resource burst is created; collector scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing stalled-tool tracking, timer disposal and per-turn reportedHangReasons suppress repeated work. The new allowlist is fixed; custom hashes are ephemeral. Undefined hang tool IDs skip normalization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracker timer thresholds, reportedHangReasons, paired completion ownership and the undefined-tool guard.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of simultaneous stalled sessions is unknown; hashing is confined to short names and existing deduplicated events.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: diagnostic frequency, timers, provider diagnostics, client-connection reads and boundary calls are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Process tool lifecycle telemetry with usage telemetry disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reporter methods still prepare events before AgentHostTelemetryService.publicLog2 rejects them by telemetry level. The diff therefore hashes custom names even when events are dropped; it does not perform any new awaited operation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One custom-name hash per invocation report, approval report or eligible diagnostic report, not per streaming delta or result character.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous per-report CPU work on the host thread, with no collector tasks scheduled for dropped usage events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fixed process-wide allowlist; no retained custom-name keys and no negative-cache behavior. Hashes are not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that hashing precedes the existing usage-level gate; service and NullTelemetryService paths do not introduce network, IPC, subprocess, database or filesystem calls for these dropped records.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Disabled telemetry does gain small unnecessary CPU work, but neither realistic event frequency nor identifier sizes establishes material user-visible degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: Omit as a finding: identifier-sized hashing before an existing gate is not independently a concrete material performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load the telemetry reporter during Agent Host startup and retain it across sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reporter module evaluation constructs one allowlist Set before the reporter can be used. The new Copilot allowlist dependency imports only tool-search constants and performs a small fixed array mapping; server tool enum references are constant literals. No runtime SDK initialization is reached by these new imports.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed code-defined tool-name set per module instance, independent of sessions, tool-call history or custom-name diversity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous module initialization; no background process, asynchronous initializer or added startup fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normal module caching reuses the allowlist for all reporter instances and sessions. No per-name cache grows over process lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from complete new import-chain inspection and the absence of dynamic additions to telemetryToolNames.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact startup allocation/time was not measured. The inspected dependency chain is constants-only and fixed in size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup or retention regression: the new state is small and bounded, and the imports do not start heavyweight work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base 60385084191c4017b47890036eabef4a92e1b570. Inspected the complete five-file inventory and every diff page, then traced reporter callers, deduplication, timers, new imports, telemetry gates, serialization, collector transport and logger ownership. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
